report.summary: Joern uses OverflowDB (custom disk-based key-value store), CodeQL uses a relational engine (Datalog-like), Glean uses RocksDB. Query patterns are traversal-heavy (call chains, def-use, control flow) demanding recursion and indexing. For embeddability, start with an in-memory model (e.g., NetworkX) with a storage abstraction layer; Kuzu or SQLite with recursive CTEs are potential disk-backed options. Avoid general graph DBs like Neo4j unless required for distributed querying.
risks: Scaling to large codebases (e.g., >100k LOC) may exceed in-memory limits; disk-based storage necessary.
Custom storage might be needed for incremental updates and specialized indexes (e.g., AST node types).
todos: Design a graph storage abstraction layer (nodes, edges, traversal API).
Implement a memory-only prototype using NetworkX on a medium-sized project.
Benchmark basic queries (call graph, control flow) to determine performance envelope.
Evaluate Kuzu or SQLite with recursive CTEs if persistence is required early.

handoff.suggestion: Start with an in-memory DiGraph (NetworkX) and a simple serialization format (e.g., JSON or MessagePack). Later, swap to OverflowDB-like key-value store if scaling demands it.
